# Droid Vault 2.0.0

The stable release. Debloat and Restore now work as a pair, and a backup can no
longer cancel itself.

## What's fixed

- **Restore can finally see what you removed.** The Restore tab read its list from
  a place that the debloat itself had just emptied, so it showed nothing. It now
  reads from your backup folder.

- **Restore no longer claims success it can't prove.** Android's unarchive
  command prints "Success" and exits 0 whether or not anything was installed.
  Restore now confirms the app is really installed and enabled before it says so.

- **"Keep Data" is on by default.** Turning it off now asks you to confirm first,
  because that one deletes the app's data for good.

- **System apps are no longer silently skipped.** They could be ticked and drawn
  with a checkmark, then left out of the backup anyway.

- **A finished backup no longer cancels the next one.** You could get "Import
  cancelled" after every single byte had copied successfully.

- **Import updates the list immediately**, instead of waiting for you to leave the
  screen and come back.

- **Partition backup and flashing wait their turn** instead of running alongside a
  backup and getting killed partway through by it.

- **A slow engine check no longer reads as "engine out of date".** It says "could
  not be checked" instead.

- **Unknown Wi-Fi security is skipped, not downgraded.** Networks that couldn't be
  identified were previously restored as open networks.

- **Automation's Add-rule sheet explains itself** when you have no labels yet,
  instead of showing an empty field and a dead button.

## Upgrading

Your backup folder is untouched. Install the APK over your existing copy — your
settings and scheduled jobs are kept.

## Download

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `arm64-v8a-release.apk` | Almost all phones from 2017 onward |
| `armeabi-v7a-release.apk` | Older 32-bit phones |

Not sure? Take the 64-bit one.

**Needs** a rooted device (Magisk, KernelSU or APatch) and Android 10+.

Please keep a second backup somewhere else. This app is built and tested by one
person, on one phone.
